newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - structure supersedes price.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - structure supersedes price.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to slightly softer in spots in late trade on Tuesday, with new issues that offered attractive features stealing the limelight.

"It's modestly softer, no great shakes," a trader said, referring to the secondary market. The market resisted slipping as much as Treasuries, just as late last week it failed to match the big gains those sister securities achieved.
"You really can't day trade municipals like you can governments, and because of that, we tend to lag," the trader explained.
Looking ahead to Wednesday, municipal bond sales that will be sold on a negotiated basis were expected to total $1.3 billion.

The top offering was a $540 million sale by the Puerto Rico Public Building Authority, follwed by a nearly $199 million sale by the New York City Local Governmental Assistance Corp. Bond sales by Puerto Rico typically see strong demand as they are triple-tax free--no federal, state or local taxes are due.
Competitive sales added up to $747 million in 24 sales.

New issues continued to capture of the market's attention, as traders said institutions preferred buying bonds that were tailor-made to meet their concerns instead of settling for a less exact match in the secondary market.
"It's really what drives the market, not absolute price, it's structure that comes first, then price," a trader said.
This proclivity in part reflects the market's failure to capture big, new sources of cash, which at present is produced chiefly from roll-overs or redemptions, he explained.
New Jersey Economic Development Authority's $115 million bond deal was repriced, lowering the yield in 2027, to about 5.564 percent from 5.60 percent.

Similarly, The School Board of Broward Coutny, Florida's $206 million sale of certificates of participation were repriced, with the top yield cut one basis point to 5.52 percent. But yields were raised in several other maturities.
Ohio's State Highway Capital Improvement sale of $125 million of bonds had a $48 million balance left in early afternoon trade.
Supplies of bonds in the secondary market dwindled from last week, with a key guage, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, totaling $906 billion, a level considered lean.
Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 100-1/4, down from 100-3/8.
And Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.56 percent, NET, down two basis points.

September municipal bond futures ended down three ticks at 116-12/32, with September Treasury bond futures slipping two ticks to 110-17/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 187 ticks, slightly firmer.
